ai.description: Brougham's earth snake reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown with a yellow lateral stripe and a blunt, shield-like tail ending in a bicarinate scale. It lacks a terminal spine.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis broughami* is best distinguished by its unique, heavily keeled, and strongly bicarinate scales on the terminal tail shield, which form a distinct, rough disc.
ai.habitat: Brougham's earth snake inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Palani Hills of the Western Ghats, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Brougham's Earth Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis broughami* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. While specific breeding data is limited, they likely reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis broughami* is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Palani Hills in the Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India.
